meta_description: When your child can't be the first to approach a new friend, how do you help? Here's a storybook about making friends with a single 'hello,' plus at-home greeting practice.

content.text:
My child hovering alone at the playground

The other kids join in and play right away, but watching your child circle at a distance all alone tugs at your heart. Their heart is full of wanting to play too, but that one word—'hi'—catches in their throat and won't come out.

Shyness isn't a flaw in your child's personality; they just need a little practice taking that first step. At times like this, one good story can open the floodgates of courage.

Curious about the making friends storybook? Take a look at its lessons alongside the illustrations. Meet the key scenes of the story too. Read it together with your child and talk it over. From a shyness storybook to a greeting storybook and a story for a bashful child, we've gathered many stories around 36. Hi! Let's Play Together!
content.caption: Shyness isn't a personality flaw—it's time to practice that first step.

content.alt: 36. Hi! Let's Play Together! - Why the courage to say hello first matters
content.text:
Why the courage to say hello first matters

The experience of reaching out first builds both confidence and social skills. A child who has tasted the success of making a friend with a single hello finds it a little easier to approach the next time.

On the other hand, always waiting for someone else to come over keeps a child in a passive place in their relationships. 'Hello' is more than good manners—it's the first step of courage in a child connecting with the world on their own.
content.caption: One hello is the first step of a child connecting with the world on their own.

content.alt: 36. Hi! Let's Play Together! - The story of bashful Bori
content.text:
The story of bashful Bori

In 『Hi! Let's Play Together!』, Bori wants to play with a new friend but only wiggles their toes. As Bori hovers alone with tears welling up, Hori comes over and says, "A greeting is just one word. 'Hi' is the key that opens the door to someone's heart!"

Bori takes a big breath and steps forward, one step, then another. In a trembling voice, Bori says, "Hi! Let's play together!"—and the new friend, Dao, breaks into a smile and answers. The three of them join hands and burst into giggles. Your child feels Bori's nerves, courage, and joy all at once.
content.caption: One trembling hello brought three friends together.

content.alt: 36. Hi! Let's Play Together! - Practicing greetings together at home
content.text:
Practicing greetings together at home

Greetings get much easier with a little practice ahead of time. Try a game of waving "Hi!" to a doll or a family member. Repeating the three steps—make eye contact, smile, say hi—like a song helps it sink into your child's body.

Before heading to the playground, set a small goal together: "How about we say hi to just one friend today?" If they succeed, praise them big; if they can't, don't push—just reassure them with "Let's try again next time."
content.caption: Make eye contact, smile, say hi—practice all three steps through play.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions

Q. How can I help when my child struggles to make friends?

A. Practice greeting first—"Hi, let's play together"—together with them. As they build up experiences of reaching out with small courage, making friends gets easier and easier.

Q. Can a making friends storybook help?

A. Watching the main character approach a friend, your child learns the courage to extend a hand first. A making friends storybook warmly conveys the thrill of meeting a new friend.

Q. Can even a very shy child make friends?

A. Respect your child's pace and gradually build up fun experiences of playing together. Without rushing, your child will make precious friends in their own way.
